Purpose of this Addendum. This Addendum supplements the published REOI by making explicit the comparative evaluation and numerical scoring methodology that will be applied to Expressions of Interest. The substantive qualification requirements already disclosed in the REOI remain unchanged.

1. Amendment to Section 4 – Shortlisting Criteria

Section 4 of the REOI is supplemented as follows:

The evaluation will be conducted in two stages.

Stage 1 – Minimum qualification requirements (Pass/Fail)

Only Consultants that satisfy the minimum requirements below will proceed to comparative scoring:

  • Relevant experience: during the last three (3) years, calculated from the date of publication of the REOI, or from the date of registration if the firm has operated for a shorter period, the Consultant must have successfully completed at least one (1) contract of the same or similar nature and complexity, with a value of at least BAM 185,000 or the equivalent in another currency.
  • Definition of a similar assignment: an assignment involving analysis of geospatial data – spatial-planning documentation, cadastral data and/or topographic data – for the purposes of mass valuation of real estate or state cadastral systems.
  • Organizational and managerial capacity: the Consultant must demonstrate adequate organizational, technical and managerial capacity to implement the assignment across all 64 local self-government units within the four-month implementation period.

A Consultant that does not satisfy the above minimum requirements will not be further evaluated.

Stage 2 – Comparative numerical scoring

Consultants that pass Stage 1 will be compared and ranked using the following scoring methodology:

No.

Evaluation criterion

Scoring guidance

Max. points

1

Core business and fields of expertise relevant to the assignment

Assessment of the extent to which the Consultant’s demonstrated core business and institutional experience are directly relevant to geospatial, cadastral, spatial-planning and/or mass valuation assignments of comparable nature. The assessment is comparative and does not introduce an additional minimum eligibility threshold.

30

2

Qualifications and experience relevant to the assignment

Assessment of the quality, relevance, depth and comparability of completed assignments demonstrated by the Consultant. Particular weight will be given to assignments involving analysis of spatial-planning, cadastral and/or topographic data for mass valuation purposes. Experience relating to state cadastral systems remains eligible in accordance with the published definition of a similar assignment, but will be assessed according to its actual relevance to the subject assignment.

60

3

Organizational, technical and managerial capacity of the firm

Assessment of the demonstrated capacity to organize and manage the assignment within the required four-month period and across all 64 local self-government units, including the firm’s organizational approach, internal coordination capacity and availability of relevant technical disciplines at firm level.

10

TOTAL

100

2. Clarification on Relevant Experience

The requirement for at least one qualifying similar contract remains a mandatory pass/fail requirement. Its purpose is to ensure that firms entering the comparative stage have demonstrated experience in assignments materially connected with the subject matter of the Study. In the comparative scoring stage, stronger and more directly relevant experience may receive a higher score, but no new minimum qualification requirement is introduced by this Addendum.

For the avoidance of doubt, direct experience in using or analysing geospatial, spatial-planning, cadastral or topographic data for mass valuation purposes will be considered more directly relevant to the present assignment than experience limited to general cadastral-system work, while both remain within the published definition of a similar assignment.

3. Key Experts

Key experts will not be evaluated at the Expression of Interest / shortlisting stage. The qualifications and experience of the proposed key experts will be considered only at the subsequent stage of the CQS process, in accordance with the Terms of Reference and the Request for Proposals. The anticipated key expert positions remain Team Leader, GIS Expert and Economist/Analyst.

4. Other Provisions

All other provisions, requirements and conditions of the original REOI remain unchanged. This Addendum forms an integral part of the REOI and shall be read together with it.

The deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest remains 16 September 2026 at 12:00 noon, local time in Banja Luka.

  1. Le Gouvernement du Bénin a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (AID) pour couvrir le coût du Programme de Gouvernance Economique pour la Délivrance des Services (PGEDS) et, a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour effectuer des paiements au titre du marché relatif au recrutement d'un consultant pour la réalisation de l’audit de l’efficacité des instruments de paiement numérisé exploité par le trésor public.
  2. Les services à fournir par le consultant (cabinet) visent principalement à améliorer l’efficacité des instruments de paiements numérisés utilisés par la Direction Générale du Trésor et de la Comptabilité Publique (DGTCP). A ce titre, le consultant devra de façon spécifique (i) évaluer la performance et l’efficacité des instruments de paiement numérisés existant à la DGTCP ; (ii) analyser la conformité légale et règlementaire de ses instruments ; (iii) identifier, évaluer et atténuer les risques possibles associés aux traitements des paiements et (iv) formuler des recommandations à la DGTCP pour améliorer le processus de paiement numérique mise en place.
  3. La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de six (6) mois à compter de la date inscrite dans l’ordre de service de démarrage.
  4. Le Coordonnateur du Programme de Gouvernance Economique pour la Délivrance des Services (PGEDS), Autorité Contractante, invite par la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt, les consultants admissibles à présenter leur candidature pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.
  5. A ce titre, les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter les services (références concernant l’exécution de contrats similaires). Les consultants devront fournir les preuves relatives à leurs expériences (attestations de bonne fin d’exécution) et tout autre document jugé nécessaire. L'ensemble des documents constitutifs du dossier de manifestation d'intérêt doivent être rédigés en français et tout document rédigé dans une autre langue doit être accompagné d'une traduction certifiée conforme en français. En cas de divergence d'interprétation, la version française fera foi.
  6. Le consultant sera sélectionné par la méthode de « Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant » décrite au paragraphe 7.11 du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale en date de juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025. A l’issue de l’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt, le consultant présentant le meilleur niveau de qualification et d’expérience en rapport avec la mission sera invité à soumettre une proposition technique et financière.
  7. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur les paragraphes 3.13, 3.15 et 3.16 de la Section III du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale qui décrivent la politique de la Banque en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  8. Des cabinets peuvent s’associer avec d’autres cabinets sous forme de groupement de firmes en vue du renforcement de leurs qualifications. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les partenaires du groupement seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat.
  9. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française et en quatre (04) exemplaires (1 original et 3 copies), portant la mention « Recrutement d'un consultant pour la réalisation de l’audit de l’efficacité des instruments de paiement numérisé exploité par le trésor public» seront déposées physiquement, à compter de la date de publication du présent avis jusqu’au _____________________ à 10 heures précises GMT + 1 (heure de Cotonou) au plus tard, au Secrétariat particulier du PGEDS sis à l’adresse ci-dessous. Toutefois, les consultants situés hors du territoire béninois peuvent transmettre leur manifestation d'intérêt par courrier électronique à l'adresse mail ci-dessous.

Les plis seront ouverts le _______________________ à 10 heures 30 min GMT+1 (heure de Cotonou) dans la salle de réunion du PGEDS en présence des consultants ou de leurs représentants qui désirent y assister.

Un Peuple – Un But – Une Foi

------------------

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT ET DE LA TRANSITION ECOLOGIQUE (METE)

-------------------

PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES AU SENEGAL (SENRM)

 

 

Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji - Dalaba dans le Parc National de Niokolo Koba (P.N.N.K)

_______________________________

 

Pays : Sénégal

Projet : Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

 Titre du Marché :  Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji-Dalaba dans le Parc national du Niokolo-Koba (PNNK)

Crédit No : 71890

Appel d’Offres No : T_SENRM/MEDDTE_013 (Réf. SYGMAP : T_SENRM_004)

 

1.     L’Etat du Sénégal a obtenu un crédit de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché relatif aux Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji-Dalaba du dans le Parc National du Niokolo-Koba (PNNK).

2.       Le Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM METE) invite, par la présente, les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles à soumettre des Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation des Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji – Dalaba dans le Parc National de Niokolo Koba PNNK pour une durée de cinq (05) mois.

3.       La passation de marchés sera conduite par passation de marchés au niveau national en utilisant un Document d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) tel que défini dans les « Règles des Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs de FPI de septembre 2025 », et est ouverte à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles.

4.       Les soumissionnaires doivent remplir les conditions de qualifications ci-après :

-        Justifier l’exécution d’au moins un marché similaire d’un montant de neuf cent vingt millions neuf cent trente-quatre mille (920 934 000) FCFA au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021 à 2025) ;

-    Produire une attestation de capacité financière ou une ligne de crédits d’un montant de trois cent quatre-vingt-trois millions sept cent vingt-deux mille (383 722 000) FCFA, délivré par un organisme bancaire ou une compagnie de cautionnement agréé par le Ministère en charge des finances ou par une institution bancaire ou de cautionnement étrangère disposant d’un correspondant local agréé par le Ministère en charge des finances.

-      Avoir un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen d’au moins un milliard sept cent vingt-six millions (1.726.000.000) F CFA, au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021 à 2025). Produire les états financiers certifiés par un expert-comptable agréé par l’ONECCA ou un organisme assimilé au cours des cinq dernières années (2021 à 2025).

 Pour les détails, veuillez consulter l’annexe A aux données particulières du dossier d’appel d’offres.

5.  Les Soumissionnaires intéressés de pays éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de la Spécialiste de Passation des Marchés du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE) ; adresse électronique : passationdemarches.senrmmeddte@gmail.com  et examiner le Document d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau de 9 :00 à 17 :00 heures à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : Projet SENRM, 7ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar.

6.       Le Document d’Appel d’Offres en Français peut être acheté par tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles en formulant une demande écrite à la Coordonnatrice du Projet et déposée au bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar contre un paiement non remboursable de cent mille (100 000) FCFA. La méthode de paiement sera par transfert WAVE, espèces ou toute autre forme de règlement acceptable. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par courriel à l’adresse électronique indiquée sur la demande ou retiré physiquement à l’adresse ci-avant indiquée.

7.      Les Offres doivent être remises au bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN Sud foire lot N°30 SIPRES Dakar au plus tard le jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. La remise des Offres par voie électronique ne sera pas permise. Toute Offre reçue après la date limite de remise des Offres sera écartée. Les Offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants désignés des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des Offres à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : Salle de réunion du Projet SENRM/METE au 7ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar le jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. Les offres devront rester valides cent-vingt (120) jours à compter de la date limite de leur dépôt.

8.       Toutes les Offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie d’Offre, pour un montant de Trente millions de francs CFA (30.000.000 frs CFA). La Garantie d’Offre devra rester valide vingt-huit (28) jours après l’expiration de la validité des offres. Elle doit être délivrée par une institution bancaire ou une compagnie d’assurance agréée par le Ministère en charge des Finances ou par une institution bancaire étrangère ayant un correspondant local agréé par le Ministère en charge des Finances.

9. Une visite du site est prévue. Elle aura lieu le mercredi 23 septembre 2026 au Parc national de Niokolo koba (PNNK). Pour plus d’informations, veuillez contacter la Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés du Projet.

Les frais engagés lors de la visite du site sont à la charge des candidats.

10.   L’(les) adresse(s) auxquelles il est fait référence ci-dessus est (sont) :

Nom de l’Agence d’exécution : Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

Nom du responsable et son titre : Mme Ndeye Coura Mbaye DIOP, Coordonnatrice du Projet

Adresse postale, le no du bureau, l’étage, le code postal, la ville, le pays: Immeuble Magnolia, 8ème étage, VDN Sud foire lot N°30 SIPRES Dakar

Numéro de téléphone et les codes de la ville et du pays : 00221 33 801 05 92/00221 78 594 82 82, CP 11500

Adresse courriel : senrm.environnement@senrm.org

Adresse du site web : senrm.senrm.org

  • Lot 1 : matériels technologiques ;
  • Lot 2 : techniques de débordement.

Le soumissionnaire peut soumettre une offre pour les lots ou le lot de son choix.

Le projet SENRM sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les matériels et outillages techniques (matériels d’évaluation des ressources forestières, outils professionnels de communication en milieu forestier) et, suivant le délai de livraison et au lieu indiqués dans le DAO.

a. Capacité financière :

- Fournir les états financiers des trois dernières années (2023, 2024, 2025) dûment certifiés par un expert-comptable ou un cabinet agréé par l’ONECCA (Ordre National des Experts Comptables et Comptables Agréés) du Sénégal ou un organisme assimilé, pour chaque lot.

- Avoir réalisé un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen au cours des trois (03) dernières années (2023, 2024 et 2025) au moins égal à :

  • Cent treize millions trois cent quatre-vingt-cinq mille (113 385 000) F CFA pour le lot 2, outillages techniques.

                           b. Capacité technique et Expérience :

Le candidat doit prouver, document à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

Prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences d’expérience ci-après : 

Deux (2) marchés similaires exécutés par le candidat au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 et 2025) pour un montant au moins égal à :

  • Quatre-vingt-dix-huit millions (98 000 000) F CFA pour le lot 1, matériels technologiques ;
  • Soixante millions quatre cent soixante-douze mille (60 472 000) F CFA pour le lot 2, outillages techniques.
  • 3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale (AON) telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale de septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.
  •  4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de la Spécialiste en passation des marchés du Projet SENRM/METE ; adresse électronique : passationdemarches.senrmmeddte@gmail.com et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau (du lundi au vendredi) de 09h 00 à 17h 00, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.
  • 5. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un dossier d’appel d’offres complet en français, en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-après : bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’immeuble Magnolia, Voie de dégagement Nord, Sud Foire, Lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar et contre un paiement non remboursable de cinquante mille (50 000) francs CFA par FAITES SIGNE DE LA MAIN. Le document d’appel d’offres sera adressé par courriel à l’adresse électronique indiquée sur la demande ou retiré physiquement à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessus. Un exemplaire du DAO sera disponible sur place pour la consultation gratuite. Par respect aux principes de transparence et d’égalité de traitement des candidats, tout candidat qui, décide de déposer une offre, devra obligatoirement payer le coût du DAO.
  • 6. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse de retrait du DAO ci-dessus, au plus tard le Mardi 06 octobre 2026, à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous, à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar, le Mardi 06 octobre 2026. Les offres devront restées valides quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à compter de la date limite de leur dépôt.
  • 7. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie de l’Offre, pour un montant de :

La Garantie de l’Offre devra restée valide vingt-huit (28) jours après l’expiration de la validité des offres.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

UKRAINE

Country: Ukraine

Program: «Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program»

Grant : TF0C5794

Project : P504171

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Development of Model Programs for Professionally Oriented Specialised Secondary Education

Contract Package ID: LEARN-1.1-CIRRICULA

Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program.

The Ministry of Education and Science intends to use part of the proceeds for consulting services, for which this REoI has been issued.

Consulting services (hereinafter referred to as "Services") include: supporting MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The expected period for the Consultant to provide services for the development of the online course is approximately 6 calendar months, starting in December 2026.

Detailed information regarding the provision of the specified Services is provided in the Terms of Reference (hereinafter referred to as "TOR"), which is attached.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (hereinafter referred to as the "Client") invites qualified consulting companies (hereinafter referred to as "Consultants") to express their interest in providing the specified Services. Interested Consultants must provide information that confirms their qualifications and experience required to perform the Services.

The evaluation of the expressions of interest provided by the Consultants will be carried out based on the following criteria:

Minimum Qualification Requirements (Pass/Fail Basis)

Failure to meet any of the requirements below shall result in disqualification.

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 3 (three) years of experience in education, curriculum development, institutional development, or related fields;
  • At least 3 (three) successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:

–       curriculum development or educational program design;

–       vocational education or education sector projects;

–       capacity building programs for education institutions.

In case of a Joint Venture / Consortium (JVCA), the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least 3 (three) years of relevant experience and participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments. The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial Capacity

  • Average annual turnover for the last 3 completed financial years shall be at least USD 150,000 or equivalent.

 In case of a JVCA: Lead Member: minimum 50% of the annual turnover requirement; Other members: minimum 25% of the annual turnover requirement; Combined: must fully meet the annual turnover requirement. Audited financial statements or verified financial documents shall be provided.

Experience with Donor-Funded Projects

  • At least one assignment financed by international financial institutions or bilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, EU, GIZ, UNICEF, etc.) within the last 5 years is an advantage.

Staff

The Consultant shall provide suitably qualified professionals in terms of expertise and time allocation to complete the activities required under the scope of work and to finally achieve the objectives of the Assignment in terms of time, costs and quality, within the agreed timeframe.

The Consultant shall also provide adequate administrative staff (secretaries, translators, etc.) needed to support the expert team.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, items 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers[1], dated September 2023 with amendments of September 2025[2] (hereinafter referred to as the "Procurement Regulations"), which contains the World Bank's policy regarding conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Selection of a Consultant will be performed in accordance with Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method following World Bank’s Consultants Guidelines.

Further information may be obtained at the address below.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in Ukrainian or English via email to the address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org; uiherp@mon.gov.ua by 2:00 PM Kyiv time on September 30, 2026.[3]

Expressions of interest to be clearly marked: "LEARN-1.1-CIRRICULA: Expression of Interest".

Consultants should provide not only information demonstrating their compliance with the Mandatory Minimum Qualification Requirements, but also information that meets the specific requirements of the assignment and will be considered an advantage. The Consultant rating will be based on compliance with these latter requirements. The Consultant with the highest rating, determined according to the established criteria for evaluating the Consultant’s qualifications, will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Information on the Consultant’s experience provided by the Consultants must be documented (copies of contracts or parts thereof, and acceptance certificates for services provided; additionally, client references may be submitted, describing the specifics of the completed assignment).

Interested Consultants are additionally advised to pay attention to the following aspects when preparing their information:

  • Files submitted by the Consultant should be in PDF (Portable Document Format) and/or JPG formats and should be as consolidated as possible;

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

 

BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA

AGRICULTURE RESILIENCE AND COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT

Project ID No. P171266

 

LOAN NO. 9359-BA

 

 

The Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina has received financing in the amount of US$ 80.0 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Agriculture Resilience and Competitiveness Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase climate resilience and competitiveness of the agriculture sector.

 

The project will include the following components:

 

  1. Component 1: Enhancing Public Support Resilience and Traceability.

 

(a)       Enhancing agriculture information systems, through, inter alia: (i) enhancement of the farm and client register, including establishing new registers, information systems and web portals, as might be necessary; (ii) development of a payment system; (iii) strengthening the existing agricultural information system; and (iv) establishment of the Farm Accountancy Data Network;

(b)       Supporting climate-resilient agriculture, through, inter alia: (i) improvement of seed quality and production, (ii) activities to increase farmers’ awareness of possible climate change impacts; and (iii) improvement of extension services delivery, including through developing of related information systems, registers and web portals, as well as providing support to producers to comply with good agricultural practices, integrated pest management and climate risk assessment and interventions in value chains;

(c)       Enhancing agriculture information system’s capacities for the benefit of MoFTER.

 

  1. Component 2: Improving Agriculture Productivity, Adaptation to Climate Change, and Enhancing Linkages with Markets.

 

(a)       Strengthening value chains and developing productive partnerships through: (i) provision of Matching Grants to eligible Beneficiaries for carrying out Matching Grant Subprojects with the aim to support: input supply, marketing of horticulture and livestock products in the internal and external markets, and increase of knowledge and capacity of the Beneficiaries; (ii) technical assistance to the Beneficiaries to comply with the market requirements; and (iii) awareness activities to promote the Matching Grants.

 

(b)       Improving irrigation and drainage systems for climate change adaptation Sub-projects, including: (i) construction of new, and rehabilitation and modernization of selected existing irrigation and drainage systems, including the preparation of the feasibility and design studies; and (ii) strengthening of irrigation and drainage management institutions, including capacity building of selected local administrative bodies, WUAs and local utility companies, development of a database of all irrigation systems and assessment of their functionalities, and development of the drainage information management system.

 

  1. Component 3: Enhancing Food Quality and Safety

 

(a)       Enhancing food quality and safety standards, through, inter alia: (i) strengthening selected food quality and safety institutions’ capacities in disease and pests controls, traceability, inspections, risk assessment, as well as laboratory capacity and testing in food safety, veterinary and phytosanitary areas; (ii) alignment with the relevant EU legislation and international standards and requirements; (iii) investments into veterinary, inspection, food quality and safety infrastructure, including  procurement of necessary laboratory and IT equipment, as well as consumables, and Training.

 

(b)       Strengthening IT systems for food safety enhancement with the purpose of alignment and compliance with EU requirements, through, inter alia, development and upgrading of IT software and hardware systems in veterinary, food safety and plant health areas.

 

(c)       Review and upgrade of the veterinary IT systems, upgrade of the phytosanitary system, and of the food safety system for the benefit of MoFTER and FSA.

 

  1. Component 4: Project Management

This Component relates to coordination, administration, monitoring and evaluation of the Project.

 

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018) (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

 

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, in UN Development Business online, on the World Bank’s external website and in leading local newspapers.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

Fraternité – Travail – Progrès

MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE ET DE L’ELEVAGE

 

PROJET D’APPUI AU DEVELOPPEMENT DES CULTURES IRRIGUEES ET A L’INTENSISIFICATION DE LA PRODUCTION ANIMALE (PACIPA)

Avis de Manifestation d'Intérêt pour le recrutement d’un Conseil en Transaction (Transaction Advisor) pour la Structuration, la Mobilisation d’Investisseurs et la Sélection d’un Partenaire Stratégique pour l’Exploitation d’un Abattoir Moderne à Vocation Exportatrice au Niger.

 

N°de référence : NE-LAMP-568937-CS-QCBS

 

Cet Avis à Manifestation d’Intérêt fait suite à la publication de l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés (AGPM) publié sur le site de la Banque Mondiale le 05 Août 2025 et sur le Sahel Dimanche du 08 Août 2025.

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a sollicité un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant du financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant :  

Recrutement d’un Conseil en Transaction (Transaction Advisor) pour la Structuration, la Mobilisation d’Investisseurs et la Sélection d’un Partenaire Stratégique pour l’Exploitation d’un Abattoir Moderne à Vocation Exportatrice au Niger.

2. Les services du Consultant (« Services ») comprennent : lire plus bas les Termes de référence.

3.  L’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA) invite les consultants admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont entre autres :

Le Cabinet devra démontrer une expérience avérée dans :

  • la structuration de Partenariat Public Privé (PPP) ;
  • les concessions et délégations de service public ;
  • la mobilisation d’investisseurs stratégiques ;
  • les transactions dans les secteurs agroalimentaires, industriels ou logistiques ;
  • les opérations d’investissement orientées vers l’exportation.

Expérience Générale

Avoir au moins quinze (15) années d’expérience de présence ou interventions internationales avérées ;

Références Spécifiques

Avoir au moins trois (03) missions comparables portant sur :

  • des abattoirs industriels ;
  • des infrastructures agroalimentaires ;
  • des PPP ou concessions ;
  • des opérations ayant abouti à la sélection effective d’un partenaire privé ;
  • Avoir au moins une mission dans laquelle le Cabinet a intégré des exigences E&S (standards IFC, NES Banque mondiale, ou Principes de l'Équateur) dans la structuration d'une transaction agro-industrielle ou d'infrastructure ;
  • Avoir une expérience en Afrique et sur les marchés du Moyen-Orient constituera un avantage majeur ;
  • Toute expérience de travail avec des institutions financières de développement (AFD, IFC, BEI, BOAD) appliquant des politiques de sauvegarde E&S sera considérée comme un avantage.

Le Cabinet mettra sur une équipe clé minimale ayant les profils ci-dessous :

Expert clé

Rôle dans la mission

Profil et qualifications minimales

Expérience spécifique requise

Mobilisation indicative

15 ans d’expérience, dont 10 ans en PPP ou investissements agro-industriels. Chef de mission d’au moins 3 missions comparables et participation à 2 transactions conclues. Expérience en Afrique subsaharienne souhaitable.

Diagnostic technique de l’abattoir, définition du modèle d’exploitation, des besoins de réhabilitation et des performances techniques attendues.

10 ans d’expérience et participation à au moins 3 projets de conception, réhabilitation ou exploitation d’abattoirs industriels.

Analyse des conditions d’accès aux marchés, des procédures SPS et douanières, des corridors logistiques et des contraintes d’exportation.

10 ans d’expérience dans le commerce de produits agricoles ou animaux. Maîtrise des procédures douanières, SPS, logistiques et d’exportation.

3 personnes-mois

Audit sanitaire, évaluation de la traçabilité, de la biosécurité et du bien-être animal, et définition des conditions d’agrément à l’exportation.

Docteur vétérinaire ou diplôme équivalent. Maîtrise des normes HACCP, du Codex Alimentarius et de l’OMSA.

10 ans d’expérience, dont 5 ans en inspection sanitaire, abattoirs ou transformation de produits animaux. Expérience des agréments sanitaires à l’exportation.

Audit de conformité halal, identification des référentiels applicables et définition de la feuille de route de certification.

Formation supérieure pertinente et qualification reconnue en audit ou certification halal.

8 ans d’expérience et participation à au moins 3 audits ou certifications d’abattoirs ou d’unités de viande. Connaissance des référentiels des marchés ciblés.

2 personnes-mois

Expert juridique PPP et concessions

Due diligence juridique, définition du montage contractuel, allocation des risques, préparation des documents de sélection et appui aux négociations.

Bac+5 en droit des affaires, droit public, droit des investissements ou domaine connexe. Maîtrise du droit OHADA.

12 ans d’expérience, dont 8 ans en PPP, concessions ou contrats d’investissement. Participation à au moins 3 transactions comparables, dont 2 conclues.

5 personnes-mois

Expert financier et modélisation économique

Élaboration du modèle financier, analyse de viabilité, détermination de la structure de financement et évaluation financière des offres.

Bac+5 en finance, économie, comptabilité ou ingénierie financière. Certification professionnelle souhaitée.

12 ans d’expérience et réalisation d’au moins 3 modèles financiers de PPP, concessions ou projets agro-industriels.

6 personnes-mois

Expert en développement des marchés et exportations

Étude des marchés, identification des débouchés et acheteurs, et élaboration de la stratégie commerciale et d’exportation.

Bac+5 en marketing, commerce, économie agricole ou agroéconomie. Français et anglais requis ; arabe souhaité.

10 ans d’expérience, dont 5 ans dans les filières animales, la viande ou les produits agroalimentaires périssables. Expérience en études de marché et stratégies d’exportation.

4 personnes-mois

Spécialiste environnemental et social (E&S)

Conduite de l’audit E&S de l’infrastructure ; évaluation de la conformité aux NES de la Banque mondiale et aux Directives EHS de la SFI ; élaboration du Plan d’action E&S ; intégration des exigences E&S dans les critères de sélection et le contrat du partenaire.

Bac+5 en environnement, sciences sociales, génie environnemental ou domaine connexe. Maîtrise obligatoire des NES 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 et 10 de la Banque mondiale et des Directives EHS de la SFI.

10 ans d’expérience dans la gestion E&S de projets agro-industriels ou d’infrastructures en Afrique subsaharienne. Expérience avec des institutions financières appliquant le CES ou les Principes de l’Équateur. La connaissance de l’agroalimentaire ou de l’industrie de la viande constitue un avantage.

4 personnes-mois

Spécialiste Hygiène-Sécurité-Environnement (HSE)

Évaluation des risques biologiques, physiques et chimiques liés à l’abattage ; audit du traitement des effluents et de la gestion des déchets biologiques ; préparation des spécifications HSE du Plan d’action E&S.

Bac+5 en HSE, génie industriel, environnement ou sécurité au travail. Connaissance des Directives EHS de la SFI relatives à la transformation de la viande et de la volaille, ainsi que des normes de l’OIT en matière de SST.

8 ans d’expérience en HSE dans des abattoirs industriels, unités agroalimentaires ou industries à risques biologiques. Expérience en gestion des effluents et déchets industriels biologiques.

3 personnes-mois

Spécialiste engagement communautaire, social et genre

Élaboration ou revue du PMPP ; conception du MGP ; analyse des impacts sur les communautés riveraines et les éleveurs ; intégration du genre et de l’inclusion dans les critères de sélection et le contrat du partenaire.

Bac+5 en sociologie, développement social, anthropologie, études de genre ou domaine connexe. Connaissance de la NES 10 et des outils de consultation et de participation.

7 ans d’expérience dans l’engagement des parties prenantes de projets agro-industriels ou d’infrastructures en Afrique de l’Ouest. Expérience en analyse genre dans le secteur agricole ou industriel.

3 personnes-mois

Total indicatif

   

55 personnes-mois

 

 4. Le recrutement du consultant sera effectué par la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC), conformément aux dispositions de passation des marchés contenues dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » de la Banque mondiale adopté en juillet 2016 et révisé en novembre 2017, en Août 2018, Novembre 2020, Septembre 2023 et Mars 2025.

4. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant.

 5. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous du lundi au jeudi de 8 heures à 17 heures et le vendredi de 8 heures à 13 heures.

6. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en français doivent être déposées sous pli fermé en personne physique ou par courrier électronique à l’adresse suivante : Quartier Koira Kano, Rue KK 41, Niamey – NIGER, Téléphone : +227 96 47 37 54/ou 88 15 55 55, au plus tard le                             25 Septembre 2026 à 12h00, avec mention dans l’objet : « Recrutement d’un Conseil en Transaction (Transaction Advisor) pour la Structuration, la Mobilisation d’Investisseurs et la Sélection d’un Partenaire Stratégique pour l’Exploitation d’un Abattoir Moderne à Vocation Exportatrice au Niger », à n’ouvrir qu’en séance.

Specific Procurement Notice (SPN)

Request for Bids

Framework Agreement(s) for Non-Consulting

(Primary Procurement, Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Procuring Agency: Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs

Country: Bosnia and Herzegovina

Name of Project: Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project (GIVE)

Framework Agreement Title: Support to SDI stakeholders to use common GIS and database tools

RFB Reference No.: A.2.2.1

Loan No.: 96760-BA

 

  1. Bosnia and Herzegovina has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project (GIVE) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under Call-off Contracts that may be awarded under the Framework Agreement (FA) for Support to SDI stakeholders to use common GIS and database tools concluded through this RFB Primary Procurement process.
  2. The Procuring Agency is undertaking this Primary Procurement with the objective of concluding a Framework Agreement (FA). The Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs acts as the sole Employer under this Framework Agreement. Through this process, the Procuring Agency now invites sealed bids from eligible and qualified Bidders for the provision of non-consulting services for support to SDI stakeholders in the installation, configuration, deployment, and operationalization of common GIS and database tools, with the aim of building technical capacity, ensuring interoperability, and enabling the effective use of geospatial data and services across SDI stakeholder institutions.
  3. The Framework Agreement to be concluded will be Single-User. The Single-User entitled to purchase under the Framework Agreement is Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs.
  4. The Framework Agreement to be concluded will be Single-Service Provider. This activity represents a key component of the ongoing SDI development process within the GIVE Project, aimed at standardizing and operationalizing the use of common open-source and interoperable GIS and database tools among SDI stakeholders in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The procurement under this RFB is designed as a Framework Agreement covering estimated service needs over the indicated implementation period. The activities and tasks expected to be performed under this Framework Agreement may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Baseline analysis of the existing IT and GIS environment at SDI stakeholder institutions, including preparation of a software version matrix and assessment of current capacities;
  • Installation, configuration, and deployment of desktop GIS tools (including QGIS or equivalent open-source GIS software) at SDI stakeholder institutions;
  • Installation, configuration, and integration of spatial database environments (including PostgreSQL/PostGIS or equivalent) for spatial data storage and management;
  • Configuration and deployment of geospatial web service platforms (including GeoServer or equivalent) enabling publication of WMS, WFS, WCS, and OGC API services;
  • Configuration and deployment of Web-GIS / portal solutions (including MapStore or equivalent) for visualization and access to spatial data services;
  • Preparation and delivery of training programs and user manuals for personnel of SDI stakeholder institutions;
  • Handover, sustainability planning, and technical support during the transition period.
  1. The selection of a FA Service Provider to be awarded a Call-off Contract will be done through a Secondary Procurement process as defined in the Framework Agreement. However, the conclusion of a Framework Agreement shall not impose any obligation on the Procuring Agency, including participating Employers, to purchase Non-Consulting services under a Call-off Contract. The conclusion of a Framework Agreement does not guarantee that a FA Service Provider will be awarded a Call-off Contract.
  2. Bidding will be conducted through International Competitive Procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023, revised February 2025 (Procurement Regulations) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.
  3. The Framework Agreement shall be concluded for a Term of 3 years from the commencement date stated in the Framework Agreement. The initial term may be extended by a maximum of two additional years.
  4. The Primary Procurement shall establish a Closed Framework Agreement.

REPUBLIC OF LIBERIA

INFRASTRUCTURE IMPLEMENTATION UNIT

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS

South Lynch Street

Legacy Economic Corridor (LECO) Project

Project ID: P518023

Request for Expressions of Interest

CONSULTANCY SERVICES:

Social Consultant - for the Preparation of ESF Instruments for the Legacy Economic Corridor Project (LECO)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

September 2, 2026

This Request for Expressions of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this project that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (www.devbusiness.com) and the World Bank website on August 17, 2026.
 

The Government of Liberia has received a Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) from the International Development Association (IDA), toward the preparation of the Legacy Economy Corridor Project (LECO) and intends to apply part of the proceeds thereof toward payments for procuring services of an Individual Environmental Consultant to carry out the Preparation of an Environmental and Social Management Framework for the Legacy Economic Corridor Project.

The objective of this assignment is to engage a qualified Social Consultant to support the IIU/MPW in preparing the social ESF instruments required for the preparation of the LECO project, in compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), particularly Environmental and Social Standards ESS1, ESS2, ESS5, ESS7, ESS8, and ESS10. The Terms of Reference can be obtained from the IIU website.

The Infrastructure Implementation Unit (IIU) now invites eligible Individual Social Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested individual consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (CV’s, Description of similar assignments, Experience in similar conditions, Availability of appropriate skills, etc.).

Qualifications, Experience and Competencies

The Individual Consultant’s educational and professional qualifications and experience will include, but not be limited to the following:

  • An advanced degree (Master's level or higher) in social sciences, sociology, anthropology, development studies, law, or a related field;
  • A minimum of 10 years of professional experience in social safeguards or social risk management in the context of infrastructure, transport and/or agriculture projects;
  • Demonstrated experience preparing ESF instruments under the World Bank ESF, specifically Resettlement Framework, Resettlement Action Plan, Stakeholder Engagement Plan, social aspects of Environmental and Social Management Framework, and Labor Management Procedures for High-risk projects;
  • Strong knowledge of ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, ESS5, ESS8, and ESS10, and their application in Liberia;
  • Experience with community consultations in fragile, post-conflict and violence-affected settings and/or with low-literacy rural communities;
  • Familiarity with SEA/SH risk management in infrastructure/transport/agriculture projects is required;
  • Experience working in Liberia or the West Africa sub-region is a strong advantage;
  • Excellent written and spoken English is required.

The attention of the interested Consultants is drawn to the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, dated February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.


Expressions of Interest must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, courier or email on or before September 16, 2026, at 16:00 hours:

South Lynch Street

1000 Monrovia, Liberia

Email: office@iiu-mpw.org with copy to emmanuel.baker.sre@iiu-mpw.org /vlarry@iiu-mpw.org

The consulting services (“the Services”) include comprehensive supervision and project management support to UHE for the implementation of contract for Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kyiv HPP / PSP, Kaniv, Kremenchuk and Seredniodniprovska Hydropower Plants, including related services (training of UHE staff). The Project envisages the installation of BESS and the creation of an energy management system (EMS) of a total capacity of 197 MW 2-h BESS across 4 abovementioned locations. Each location and project Site is to be tendered as a separate Lot (meaning that each separate location might have their own separate contractor and their own separate contract with terms that might differ from the other), but construction is to be carried out simultaneously. Potential participants should keep in mind that they might have to deal with up to 4 different contractors and their own specific contracts during the implementation of this project. The Contract(s) is foreseen to commence on 01/02/2027, for an estimated duration of: from Effective Date until Operational Acceptance (DSI schedule, ~18 months), plus Defects Liability Period (DLP) as defined in DSI contract (forty-two (42) months from the date of Completion of the Facilities or thirty-six (36) months from the date of Operational Acceptance of the Facilities, whichever first occurs). Total estimated duration – 54 months.

PJSC "Ukrhydroenergo" now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The purpose of this Request for Expressions of Interest is to establish a shortlist of qualified consulting firms. The Request for Proposals, including the detailed evaluation methodology and contract conditions, will be issued only to shortlisted firms.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (November, 2020 edition)  (“Procurement Regulations”)and as further specified in the Request for Proposals.

The shortlisting criteria are:

Relevant experience and qualifications of the Consultant:

  • At least 10 years of experience in providing consulting services in technical supervision of construction and project management support, including on project environmental and social support;
    • Including at least two (2) projects related to installation and commissioning of BESS (as stand-alone or as part of hybrid PV/Wind + BESS projects) in the past five (5) years, each with a power and energy capacity of at least 50 MW and at least 50 MWh respectively;
    • Including at least two (2) projects related to installation and commissioning of HV substations (110 kV or higher), in the past five (5) years;
  • Experience in implementing at least four contracts/assignments related to environmental and social support for projects in the energy sector over the past seven (7) years, including at least two (2) with IFIs participation (IBRD, EBRD, ADB, etc.);

Experience under IFI-funded projects (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, KfW, ADB or similar) is acceptable; specific prior experience under WB Plant contracts is not mandatory, provided that equivalent supply-install (Plant-like) supervision experience is demonstrated.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Key Experts shall be proposed and evaluated at the Request for Proposals stage by shortlisted firms. The shortlist will contain up to 5 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Further information can be obtained by sending respective request to the e-mails provided below.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form in Ukrainian or English via email to the following address: o.hryshchenko@uhe.gov.ua, mandatory copy to ya.lykhatska@uhe.gov.ua and yu.makukha@uhe.gov.ua by 5:00 p.m. Kyiv time, September 9th, 2026 (deadline extended).[1] Expressions of Interest shall be submitted with the following reference in the subject line: “UHE-IPSR-ES: Expression of Interest”.

In order to facilitate the preparation and submission of the relevant information, the Consultants are proposed to use the following template for the preparation and submission of the Expressions of Interest (available at the following link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-nEllWAr4J593llSS--zfkIU_Hk6E_dr?usp=drive_link). At the same time, the Consultants may, at their own discretion, formulate and present relevant information in any form that, in the Consultant’s opinion, reflects the Consultant’s vision of presenting their qualifications and experience for the services provision best of all.

Consultants that will provide not only the information confirming their compliance with the qualification requirements, but also be able to demonstrate the ability to perform the tasks as stated in the Terms of Reference and meet the stated per-expert requirements as per ToR will be at advantage during the selection process. The Consultants will be ranked based on the above.

The information about the Consultant’s experience provided by the Consultant shall be confirmed by documentary evidence (copies of contracts or parts thereof and service acceptance certificates, and possibly clients’ references disclosing the specifics of the assignment performed may also be provided).

Additionally, attention of the interested Consultants is drawn to the following aspects of preparing their information:

  • the files sent by the Consultant shall be in PDF (Portable Document Format) and/or JPG formats and must be grouped logically, as much as possible;
  • in the process of preparing the information that describes your qualification and experience, please, maximize disclosure of information confirming the compliance with the established qualification criteria and the assignment specifics.
  • please, enclose copies of documents, that evidence the indicated experience and competence; also, provide contact details of third parties who can confirm your experience and provide relevant references.

Expressions of Interest submitted after the deadline may not be accepted by the Client for consideration if the list of Consultants with the required qualifications has already been formed up by that time.

The Consultants who already submitted their Expressions of Interest shall not submit any documents or information after the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, except for the cases when they provide relevant documents and/or information at the request of the Client to clarify or specify the submitted Expressions of Interest.

Any communications between the Client and the Consultants shall be made in writing via the official e-mail addresses specified herein.

De façon spécifique et afin de veiller à l'opérationnalisation performante des orientations de la Refondation en appui des organes prévus par l'arrêté ministériel, le Consultant sera chargé (e) de:

  • doter la Refondation d'un cadre méthodologique intégré de pilotage opérationnel dans les quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours suivant le début de la mission ;

  • assurer un suivi consolidé de l'exécution et de la mobilisation des ressources, avec des rapports acceptés dans les délais convenus ;

Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71–ou par email : bm.papse@education.sn, adressé au Coordonnateur du PAPSE, avec la mention « AMI N° SN-MEN-546836-CS-QCBS / C_PAPSE_239-Recrutement d'un Consultant individuel pour appuyer le comité technique de la Refondation du Système Éducatif Sénégalais», au plus tard  le mercredi 16 septembre 2026 à 10 h00mn TU.
